gloss: to come along; to arrive; to show up

definitions.gloss: to come along; to arrive; to show up
definitions.explanation: Someone or something comes to a place, with a nuance of finally arriving or appearing. Often used for people visiting or arriving at a location.

definitions.gloss: to come (of a time, season, or event)
definitions.explanation: A time period, season, or event arrives or approaches. Used for abstract things that come with the passage of time.

examples.japanese: {友達|ともだち}がやって{来|き}た。
{遠|とお}くから{観光客|かんこうきゃく}がやって{来|く}る。
{野良猫|のらねこ}が{毎日|まいにち}うちの{庭|にわ}にやって{来|く}るので、{名前|なまえ}を{付|つ}けてしまった。
examples.english: A stray cat comes to our garden every day, so I ended up giving it a name.

examples.japanese: もうすぐ{春|はる}がやって{来|く}る。
ついに{試験|しけん}の{日|ひ}がやって{来|き}た。
examples.english: The day of the exam has finally arrived.

examples.japanese: {待|ま}ちに{待|ま}った{夏休|なつやす}みがやって{来|き}て、{子|こ}どもたちは{大喜|おおよろこ}びだ。
examples.english: The long-awaited summer vacation has arrived, and the children are overjoyed.

notes:
USAGE:
More vivid and emphatic than simply {来|く}る. Suggests that the arrival takes some effort or distance, or that it is notable or eagerly anticipated. Very common in both spoken and written Japanese.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {春|はる}がやって{来|く}る (spring comes)
- {客|きゃく}がやって{来|く}る (a guest arrives)
- ついにやって{来|き}た (it finally arrived)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {来|く}る: to come — neutral and general, while やって{来|く}る adds emphasis or a sense of distance
